entities.summary:
The October Revolution was a pivotal event in modern history that took place in Saint Petersburg, Russia, on November 7-8, 1917. This second revolution in 1917, led by the Bolshevik Party, led to the overthrow of the provisional government and the establishment of a socialist state, marking the beginning of the Soviet era. The revolution was sparked by widespread discontent with the provisional government and the failures of the Russian economy, which had been ravaged by World War I. The Bolsheviks, led by Vladimir Lenin, seized power and established a new government, which would go on to shape the course of Russian and world history for decades to come.

The October Revolution was a turning point in the history of Russia, marking the end of the provisional government and the beginning of the Soviet era. The revolution was characterized by mass protests, street fighting, and the eventual seizure of power by the Bolsheviks. The revolution led to the establishment of a socialist state, which would go on to shape the course of Russian and world history for decades to come. The October Revolution also had a profound impact on the course of the Russian Civil War, which would go on to shape the course of Russian history for decades to come.

The legacy of the October Revolution can be seen in the establishment of the Soviet Union, which would go on to become one of the world's most powerful empires. The revolution also had a profound impact on the course of communism, which would go on to shape the course of world history for decades to come.
